theorem_title: Scaling of finite height in a number field extension
preamble:
import Definitions.Def_TripodCanonicalHighHeightInputs

set_option autoImplicit false

open AbcAdaptation.Tripod
open NumberField
formal_statement:
theorem AbcAdaptation.Tripod.finHeight_algebraMap {k K : Type*} [Field k] [NumberField k] [Field K] [NumberField K]
    [Algebra k K] (y : k) :
    finHeight (algebraMap k K y) = Module.finrank k K * finHeight y := by sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $K/k$ be an extension of number fields, and let $y\in k$. The finite height $h_{\mathrm{fin},K}$ is the sum of the positive parts of the logarithms of the absolute values at the finite places of $K$. When $y$ is viewed in $K$, the height satisfies

$$h_{\mathrm{fin},K}(y)=[K:k]\,h_{\mathrm{fin},k}(y).$$

This is the base-extension step in the comparison between the heights of the supplied curve and its point field.
